lang: How do you say hello in Japan?

pages.head: Hello around the world
text: Every country has its own way to say hello. In the UK and the USA, people usually say "Hello" or "Hi" and shake hands. They also ask, "How are you?" but they do not expect a long answer. You just say, "I'm fine, thanks. And you?"
In Japan, people bow. The bow can be short for friends and deep for a boss or a teacher. In Brazil, friends often kiss on the cheek. In India, many people put their hands together and say "Namaste".
A smile is the same everywhere. So when you don't know what to do, smile and say "Hello!"
tf: In the UK and the USA, people usually shake hands.
In Japan, people kiss on the cheek.
A smile is only for friends.

pages.talk: How do people greet each other in your country?

pages.title: Greetings: fact file

facts.label: people speak English
facts.sub: as a first or second language

text: 'How are you?' is usually just a greeting. The answer is short.
In English-speaking countries, people say 'Good morning' to neighbors, bus drivers and shop assistants. It is polite and friendly.
'Hi' and 'Hey' are fine with friends. Use 'Hello' or 'Good morning' with your boss or in a shop.
